proof_summary: For triples satisfying \(m=n(k+1)+(n+1)j\), the involution \((n,k,j)\mapsto(k+j,k,n-k)\) pairs contributions with equal binomial weight modulo \(2\), so nonfixed terms cancel. A fixed point has \(n=k+j\): if \(j=0\) then \(m=n(n+1)\), while for \(j>0\) its weight is even because it contains, via a binomial product identity, the even central binomial coefficient \(\binom{2j}{j}\).
